messages:
Maria L.: Quick sync — goal for this thread: finalize copy and inbound routing for the launch posts + webinar funnel across Hosted / Dedicated / Private pages. I sketched an inbound matrix and a couple of headline variants. Can we do a quick pass?
Jack S.: Sounds good. Share the matrix?
Maria L.: https://docs.redwood.ai/rd/edge-launch-matrix (draft) — routing rules: free trial -> hosted sign-up, high-touch lead -> demo request (Dedicated/Private), benchmarks -> download + webinar reg CTA. Thoughts on headline pairings?
Anya (growth): Love the routing. For headlines: 1) "Production-grade LLM inference, without the ops" 2) "Predictable performance for every deployment: Hosted, Dedicated, Private" — prefer #2 for enterprise clarity.
Ollie: #2 reads safer. For hosted hero we should keep lean: "Start with Hosted — get results fast." For Dedicated/Private hero copy, lead with "SLA-backed" or "VPC-ready" phrasing.
Jack S.: Agree. Also recommend a 2-line subhead for each mode that includes a metric callout (latency/cost). e.g., "< 50ms p95. Save 3x per-token vs naive serving."
Anya (growth): Can we avoid numeric claims until we have benchmark pages? Maybe use relative phrasing: "latency and costs you can plan around." Then link to a benchmark report page as social proof.
Maria L.: Good catch — we'll keep numbers out of top-level copy. Subheads: Hosted: "Fast time-to-value with our hosted API" Dedicated: "Predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools" Private: "Control and compliance for regulated workloads"
Ollie: For CTA paths, here's a recommended mapping: Hosted -> "Start free" (UTM: utm_campaign=launch&utm_medium=website&utm_source=hosted), Dedicated -> "Request capacity" (form), Private -> "Contact sales" (SLA/enterprise lead).
Jack S.: Add a joint CTA on the benchmark page: "See real-world latency & cost comparisons" -> gated download/webinar reg. Use the webinar as the primary lead-gen for Dedicated/Private.
Anya (growth): Webinar plan: 45min product + 15min live Q&A. Target audience: infra/platform engineers, ML infra leads, startup CTOs. Promotion cadence: 2 announcement posts, 2 reminder posts, 1 day-before, and email to trialers.
Maria L.: Draft social posts? I tried two tones: a) technical: "Benchmarking inference: how to get cost predictability across Hosted, Dedicated, Private — join our webinar" b) value: "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and cost — live demo + benchmarks" Which to A/B?
Ollie: Use technical for gated benchmark audience, value for broader sign-ups. Also include a short testimonial quote on the landing page (one-liner) — can use anonymized beta customer quote: "Cut inference costs and hit p95 targets in days."
Jack S.: Landing layout idea: hero > three-mode cards with subhead + CTA > benchmark highlight (download + webinar) > technical bullets (batching, KV caching, smart routing) > customer quote > footer form.
Anya (growth): For inbound matrix: add a rule — if user clicks "Request capacity" and uses corporate email, tag as enterprise_lead and route to AE queue via HubSpot. If trial signup with personal email, route to product nurture.
Maria L.: Perfect. Next steps: I will update copy in the live draft (docs) and create two social post variants. Ollie — can you wire the UTM links and the routing rules in the sheet? Jack — can you add the benchmark gating flow and sample webinar reg form?
Ollie: Yep, I'll add UTM mapping and HubSpot rules by EOD. :white_check_mark:
Jack S.: I'll mock the reg form and gating logic by tomorrow morning.
Anya (growth): I'll prepare the email cadence and write the two post drafts.
launch-bot: Webinar created: "Launch Benchmarks: Inference at Scale" on 2026-04-07 16:00 UTC — registration link: https://events.redwood.ai/benchmarks-webinar
Maria L.: Thanks team. We'll reconvene after the drafts are in. If anyone has objections to the routing matrix or headline pairs, flag here. :rocket:
